ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows N≡N on the reactant side plus three H-H molecules, with an arrow pointing to two NH3 molecules on the product side. Reasoning: On the reactant side, N2 contains 2 nitrogen atoms and the three H2 molecules contain 6 hydrogen atoms total. On the product side, two NH3 molecules contain 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms total. Because the numbers of each kind of atom are the same before and after the reaction, the diagram supports the conclusion that mass is conserved in chemical reactions.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the chemical diagram: on the left there is one N≡N molecule and three H-H molecules; on the right there are two ammonia-like molecules, each with one N bonded to three H atoms. Count 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms on both sides of the reaction arrow.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question prompt to know the task is to state the conclusion supported by the diagram about the reaction, not to calculate a numeric mass or identify the compound name.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the law of conservation of mass: if the same numbers of each type of atom appear in reactants and products, no atoms are created or destroyed, so total mass is conserved in the chemical reaction.
